title: Trains to Redditch
from: stations across the Midlands and beyond
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Midlands Air Festival at Ragley Hall. Redditch is the station I would use. It’s the end of the Cross City line, with West Midlands Railway trains every half an hour or so through Birmingham, and from there the Diamond 247 bus to Evesham stops right by the Ragley Hall main entrance. The bus is the part to plan around, as it’s not frequent and doesn’t run on Sundays. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
facts: Cross City line, about every 30 minutes
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the festival. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From Redditch, the Diamond 247 bus to Evesham stops right by the Ragley Hall main entrance. In the current timetable there are only three buses each way on a Saturday and none on a Sunday or a bank holiday, so please check the bus times before you rely on it. From the main entrance it’s about 1.5 miles to the house, so wear comfortable shoes.
walkBack: In the current timetable the last 247 bus back to Redditch passes Ragley at about 18:00, which is well before the evening balloons and the Nightfire. I would check the last bus before you go, then pick your train home from Redditch.
tip: The 247 bus is the part to plan. With only a few buses and nothing on a Sunday, I would look at the bus times first and work your train back from them.
If you want the Friday Nightfire or the evening balloons, the last bus back leaves too early, so I would plan another way home before you set off.
Weekend engineering works around Birmingham are common, and the summer 2027 times come out nearer the festival, so please check before you travel.

Walk to Aldgate, about 5 minutes from Fenchurch Street, and take the Circle or Metropolitan line to Euston Square. Euston is a short walk from there.

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go on the long legs, but it ties you to one train. With a bus to fit in, I would book a flexible ticket for the way home.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a festival when you don’t know when you’ll leave. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.
A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Redditch. It’s the most suitable station for the festival, and the Diamond 247 bus from there stops right by the Ragley Hall main entrance.
Does the bus run every day?
No. In the current timetable the 247 has no Sunday or bank holiday service, and only three buses each way on a Saturday, so please check the bus times before you rely on it.
Can I stay for the Nightfire or the evening balloons?
The last 247 bus back passes Ragley at about 18:00, well before the evening balloons and the Nightfire, so I would plan another way home if you want to stay.
Yes. Tickets are advance only, with none on the gate. In 2027 a one day adult ticket is £35.97, and children 12 and under go free.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
access: Trains can work really well for the festival, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
It’s about 1.5 miles from the main entrance to the house, so please plan for the walk, and take a look at the festival’s accessibility details before you book.
